_: A registered hook answers a faulty edit and passes a clean one. This says which edit is which. `check_hooks` runs
the pair against the command `.claude/settings.json` registers. A hook that answers neither reads as silent. A
hook that answers both cannot tell a faulty edit from a clean one.
A hook takes a list of pairs. `probes` names what the pair puts the fault in. A hook reading a comment and a
string literal gets a pair apiece. An arm no pair fires against goes untried.
This is data rather than Python. The hooks refuse the faults below. A hook that reads a module of `generator/`
would find such a fault in the source of the check that runs it.
`TREE` in a path names the root of the repository. The Edit tool hands an absolute path. A hook matching
`*/x/*.py` answers nothing about a relative one.
A pair with a `file` fires as an edit into that text. `check_hooks` writes the text under a scratch directory by
its basename. The payload is then the Edit the tool would send. Its `old_string` cuts a slice out of a line, with
no comment marker in the slice. A hook reading that slice sees no prose and passes.
